I farm only 4.1 mu, and my household labor is limited because some family members work off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple and familiar. I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because I know it well, it matches my irrigation conditions, and it gives me steady grain output across the year. I will keep a smaller piece in cotton because I already grow it, but I will not expand it too much since cotton needs more field watching and more pesticide sprays. With well irrigation at the start of the season, I will rely on improved or hybrid seed, moderate fertilizer, and a manageable number of irrigations and sprays rather than chasing the highest possible input level. For wheat I will use stable fertilizer and two irrigations because that is the crop I depend on for a safe harvest. After wheat, I will direct-seed summer maize on the same land with a slightly lighter water schedule and keep tillage lighter to save labor. For cotton, I will keep the area smaller, feed it with more potassium than grain crops, irrigate several times, and control insects more closely because cotton is more sensitive to pest pressure here.
